reader_A.evidence: Re-measured TRUE: SAMEKH on 29:7; one K/Q pair on 29:7 (בכפך / בַכַּף֙); 29:8 opens לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה and addresses a 2fs (עָלַ֖יִךְ, מִמֵּ֖ךְ); 29:7 addresses a 2ms (בְּךָ֤, עָלֶ֨יךָ֙); no dateline or word-event in 29:2-29:16; 29:9's recognition ends at the etnachta and יַ֧עַן אָמַ֛ר follows as an independent clause; 29:6's remainder is יַ֧עַן הֱיוֹתָ֛ם (infinitive construct); 29:6 is in the 64 family but not the strict 28. FALSE (1): '... so this rival is licensed and two-faced ... Its far face is nevertheless thin: MT 29:7 ends with no close-role formula, so the second would fail there and only the SAMEKH stands.' By the unified definitions a rival is two-faced only when its far face ENDS on a close-role signal, and marks make no face. The sentence measures that 29:7 has none, then calls the rival two-faced; the grade sentence repeats 'A licensed two-faced rival'. The 29:7/29:8 rival is licensed (addressee change), not two-faced. Medium still follows from the licensed limb. FALSE by omission (2): 'MEASURED in this witness, the only marks inside that stretch follow MT 29:7 and MT 29:12'. The stretch is defined as 'between MT 29:1 and the next dateline at MT 29:17', and pmarks also records a PE on MT 29:16, which is exactly the close of alternative (3). Under the mark-disclosure vocabulary a mark on a 29:1-16 row's last verse stands at its close seam, so the sentence is true only in that reading. Either way the rejected-alternative field never names the 29:16 PE that corroborates alternative (3).

row_level_defects.what: The SRA calls the 29:7/29:8 rival 'licensed and two-faced' and grounds medium on 'A licensed two-faced rival', while stating that its far face 29:7 ends with no close-role formula and 'only the SAMEKH stands'. Marks make no face, so the rival is licensed, not two-faced.

'the only marks inside that stretch follow MT 29:7 and MT 29:12', for the stretch between 29:1 and 29:17, omits the PE on MT 29:16 at the close of alternative (3). The field never names that mark as corroboration for the alternative.

reader_B.evidence: True: SAMEKH on 29:7 and 29:12 only inside 29:1-29:16, none on 29:9; no dateline or word-event between 29:1 and 29:17; 29:7 is 2ms (בְּךָ, וּבָקַעְתָּ, עָלֶיךָ) and 29:8 2fs (עָלַיִךְ, מִמֵּךְ); 29:8 opens לָכֵן כֹּה אָמַר אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה; 29:9's recognition ends at the etnachta and יַעַן אָמַר ... (finite) follows; 29:6's remainder יַעַן הֱיוֹתָם is an infinitive phrase; K/Q on 29:4 and 29:7. LOW: the SRA says the 29:7/29:8 rival 'is licensed and two-faced' and in the next sentence that 29:7 'ends with no close-role formula ... only the SAMEKH stands'; under the binding rival definition a far face with a mark only makes the rival licensed but not two-faced, so 'two-faced' (and 'A licensed two-faced rival held on stated grounds leaves the boundary evidence at medium') is false as written. The refrain-grade close (verse-final 2mp recognition, וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה) stands on MT 36:11. MT 36:12 continues the promise (ends וְלֹא תוֹסִ֥ף ע֖וֹד לְשַׁכְּלָֽם), carries no close-role formula, and carries only the samekh. row_level_defects.what: The rationale places 'the refrain-grade close' on MT 36:12 as the onset's far face. The verse-final recognition refrain stands on 36:11; 36:12 carries only a samekh.

reader_B.evidence: MEDIUM: the onset sentence REPAIR-2 edited says 36:13 'opens immediately after the refrain-grade close and samekh mark at oshb:Ezek.36.12 ... satisfying the seam condition from this side as well as from the close side', and refs[9] (re-qualified by REPAIR-2) reads 'web:Ezek.36.12 [WARRANT-onset:far] close and samekh behind onset'. MEASURED: the refrain (verse-final 2mp recognition) stands on MT 36:11; MT 36:12 (וְהוֹלַכְתִּי ... וְלֹא תוֹסִף עוֹד לְשַׁכְּלָם) carries no formula - only the SAMEKH. The verse immediately before 36:13 therefore does not end on a close-role formula, so 'the seam condition ... from the close side' is not met on the bytes, and the far-face warrant on 36:12 asserts a close that verse does not carry (refs[0] correctly says 'the 36.11-12 close'). True: all separator counts and Qere forms; 36:14 and 36:15 carry the utterance formula; SAMEKH on 36:15; 36:16 strict word-event.

The close sentence likewise says 23:36 'shifts to a dual/plural addressee (both sisters together)', but 23:36 addresses the prophet (וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י בֶּן אָדָ֕ם הֲתִשְׁפּ֥וֹט, 'and YHWH said to me, son of man, will you judge') with the sisters as third-person objects.
